what_this_is: The formats a post can take beyond the SDK's plain publish, as DATA. A post whose value.format names one of these is sent by its steps (read-data/publish-by-format.mjs) after the consent gates and the place checks of tool:send-a-post; every other post keeps the SDK route. A new format is a new entry here and nothing else. A carousel lists its children (one entry per item kind); follow_with names a format sent after the main post publishes, from a cover image the caller gives.

instagram.why: Instagram login (the place row's flavor): the account's own Graph origin, the one the SDK's instagram publisher uses (dist/platforms/instagram.js, apiVersion v25.0).

reel.label: Instagram trial reel

container.why_trial: A trial reel goes first to non-followers. SS_PERFORMANCE graduates it to the grid and feed automatically when it performs; MANUAL needs the native app, so the API cannot graduate it. The SDK's publishReel has no trial_params field, so this format's container is made here, with the trial settings.

reel.source: graph.instagram.com/v25.0 media and media_publish; media_type REELS with trial_params (live proof Nov 21 2026, container 18079563326737976 FINISHED after one status ask).

follow_with.why_no_link_sticker: The SDK's Instagram story publisher has no link sticker field and the Graph container call used here sends none; the cover story is posted plain, with no link to the new post.

story.label: Instagram story
story.why_own_wait: The SDK's publishStory creates the container and makes one status check; an IN_PROGRESS container answers processing and is left for a resume that this send never makes. So a story waits here.
story.source: graph.instagram.com/v25.0 media with media_type STORIES (live proof Nov 21 2026: image and video story containers accepted, video FINISHED after one status ask).

carousel.label: Instagram carousel
carousel.why_children_wait: Each child container is processed in the background as well, and a CAROUSEL container made from a child that is not FINISHED is refused by Instagram. So every child is waited on before the carousel container is made, and the carousel is waited on before media_publish.
carousel.source: graph.instagram.com/v25.0 media with is_carousel_item children and a CAROUSEL container, the same shape the SDK's publishCarousel makes (dist/platforms/instagram.js), with each step waited on here.
